outcomes.text: Distinguish a word’s category from the category of the whole phrase.
Find the heads of adjective, adverb and prepositional phrases.
Identify what is joined in a simple coordination and label the whole group.

opening.prompt: Which words does “they” replace in “The glass jars fell”?

options.feedback: “The glass” would be left behind.
The pronoun takes the place of the entire subject group.
That includes part of the predicate.

opening.prompt: Which word supplies the basic description in “very cold”?

options.feedback: “Very” indicates degree.
“Cold” can supply the description on its own.
“Cold” supplies the description and “very” adjusts its degree.

opening.prompt: Which word tells how someone spoke in “spoke rather softly”?

options.feedback: “Softly” tells how the person spoke.
“Rather” modifies “softly”.
“Spoke” names the action.

opening.prompt: In “The puppy hid behind the couch”, which group answers “Where did the puppy hide?”

options.feedback: That names the landmark.
The answer includes the relation and its landmark.
This includes the action and omits the landmark.

opening.prompt: In “The cats and the dogs slept”, which two groups does “and” join?

options.feedback: Each noun belongs to a larger group with “the”.
“Slept” is outside the coordinated subject.
Each group names one set of animals.

closing.prompt: In “Lea nodded”, how does the Chapter 3 tree represent “Lea”?

options.text: A name inside a one-word NP
options.feedback: The name supplies the whole subject NP.
The phrase level still appears above the name.
“Lea” is a name. A pronoun could replace the NP.

closing.prompt: In “The notice was unusually clear”, what is the category of the whole group “unusually clear”?

options.feedback: “Unusually” modifies the adjective.
The adjective “clear” heads the whole phrase.
A labels the head word “clear”. AP labels the phrase.

closing.prompt: In “The guide answered very patiently”, what is the head of “very patiently” and what is the group’s category?

options.feedback: “Very” marks degree. “Patiently” heads the group.
“Patiently” is an adverb in this sentence.
The adverb heads the group and “very” modifies it.

closing.prompt: Compare “The bag is under the desk” and “The bag is there”. Which phrase category covers both locations in this analysis?

options.feedback: “Under” takes an NP complement. Locative “there” can form a PP by itself here.
“The desk” is an NP inside the longer PP.
This analysis treats locative “there” as P heading a one-word PP.

closing.prompt: In “The hikers rested beside the stream and near the bridge”, what does “and” join?

options.feedback: Each noun belongs to an NP within a larger location phrase.

options.text: Two whole PPs forming a PP
options.feedback: Each conjunct includes its own preposition and landmark.

options.text: Two prepositions with one shared landmark
options.feedback: Each preposition has its own landmark group.
